quests.contextSentence: Mr. Okoye told his colleague Dana that he would send her the figures himself, since her team had lost its copy.
quests.ruleExplanation: The pronoun 'its' is non-human, so it cannot be Dana. A team can lose a copy, while the figures are what is being replaced.
quests.nativeTip: What can lose a copy, and which noun is non-human?

quests.contextSentence: The lecturers asked the graduate assistants to mark the scripts themselves, because the external examiner, who was abroad, couldn't look at them until March.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Themselves' is the assistants, so 'them' is different. The examiner cannot look at the scripts until March.
quests.nativeTip: Who cannot look at what? Who is 'themselves'?

quests.contextSentence: The volunteers who had served at the fair thanked the organisers, who in turn congratulated themselves on a smooth day.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Who in turn' refers to the organisers, who are the subject of 'congratulated'. 'Themselves' returns to the same group, not the volunteers.
quests.nativeTip: 'Who in turn' shifts the subject. Who is congratulating?

quests.contextSentence: The Hendersons rent the flat above ours. Their kitchen shares a wall with our bedroom, so we hear their dishwasher at night, and we've asked them to turn it off before eleven.
quests.ruleExplanation: Remember that 'it' refers to the device that makes noise at night. A kitchen or bedroom is a room, not something switched off.

quests.contextSentence: The sponsors withdrew their funding after the club's chairman admitted that its accounts had been altered.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Its' is non-human singular, so it is not the chairman. The accounts belong to the club that the chairman leads.

quests.contextSentence: Anna's neighbour offered to look after the cat while she was away. It had been sick the week before, and she wanted him to watch for symptoms.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'It' is non-human, so the neighbour ('him') is not the referent. The cat is the animal being looked after.

quests.contextSentence: Anyone who has ordered a product that was later recalled can claim a full refund; those who have already returned it will be paid automatically.
quests.ruleExplanation: Consider the form of 'it': it is what was ordered and can be returned. The refund is what is paid, and 'anyone' is a person.
quests.nativeTip: What could a customer send back to the shop?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'it' points back to ➔ 'the recalled product'

quests.contextSentence: Most of the committee members, several of whom had served for a decade, opposed the change, which they saw as an attack on their independence.
quests.ruleExplanation: The pronoun 'which' follows the noun just before the comma. The change is what they opposed and what they interpreted as an attack.
quests.nativeTip: What did they see as an attack?

quests.contextSentence: Neither of the two experts whom the court had appointed could explain why the readings differed, and each blamed the other's equipment for it.
quests.ruleExplanation: Note that 'it' is what is being blamed on the equipment. That is the difference in readings, not the equipment or the court.
quests.nativeTip: What did each blame the equipment for?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'it' points back to ➔ 'the difference in the readings'

quests.contextSentence: Mr. Kwon asked the driver, who was carrying the crates that had arrived that morning, where he wanted them left.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Them' is plural. The driver is singular, so it is the crates that will be left.

quests.contextSentence: The architect showed the couple two designs and explained that the cheaper one, though it used less glass, would let in more light than they expected.
quests.ruleExplanation: Remember that 'it' is inside the phrase about the cheaper design. It is the cheaper one that uses less glass, and the couple are 'they'.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'it' points back to ➔ 'the cheaper design'

quests.contextSentence: The builder told the neighbours who had complained about the dust that he would hose down the path himself.
quests.ruleExplanation: Here, 'himself' is masculine singular and stresses who does the job. The builder is the only such person; the neighbours are plural.
quests.nativeTip: Who will do the hosing down?

quests.contextSentence: The founders, who had built the company themselves, refused to sell it to investors who wanted to break it up.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Themselves' emphasises who did the building. The relative clause 'who had built' points to the founders.

quests.contextSentence: Neither Lena nor her colleagues had expected the client to accept the offer, so when it did, they were as surprised as she was.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'When it did' means 'when it accepted', so 'it' is whoever accepts. The client accepts the offer; the offer does not accept itself.

quests.contextSentence: The students told their advisor they had found the error, and that it had been in the original dataset all along.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'It' was in the dataset, so it cannot be the dataset itself. It is the error that was found.
quests.nativeTip: What had been in the dataset?

quests.contextSentence: My printer is faster than Talia's, but hers has a scanner, which mine lacks.
quests.ruleExplanation: Notice that 'which' follows 'a scanner' and comments on it. The speaker's printer lacks that feature.

quests.contextSentence: Ms. Doyle inherited two houses from her uncle, and she has decided to sell the one whose roof leaks and keep the other for herself.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Whose roof leaks' describes 'the one', which is the house she will sell. The other house is the one she keeps.
quests.nativeTip: Which house has the leaking roof, and what does 'the one' mean?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'whose' points back to ➔ 'the house she will sell'

quests.contextSentence: The tenants' association wrote to the landlord, whom it had warned twice, asking him to meet its members.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Its' is non-human, so it is not the landlord, who is 'him'. The association has members and wrote the letter.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'its' points back to ➔ 'the tenants' association'

quests.contextSentence: The tribunal found that the employer, whose managers had ignored several warnings, had failed in its duty of care.
quests.ruleExplanation: In this sentence, 'its' is the employer's duty. The tribunal only makes the finding, and the managers are plural.
quests.nativeTip: Who owes a duty of care?

quests.contextSentence: Both parties accepted the mediator's proposal, but neither believed it would resolve the underlying dispute, which had lasted a decade.
quests.ruleExplanation: Look closely: 'which' refers to the dispute. 'It' is the thing that might resolve it, and the proposal is the subject of that doubt.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'it' points back to ➔ 'the mediator's proposal'

quests.contextSentence: The author thanks the reviewers whose comments improved the manuscript and acknowledges that any errors that remain are hers alone.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Hers' is singular and feminine, so it cannot be the plural reviewers. The author accepts the remaining errors as her own.

quests.contextSentence: 'Did you give Tariq the tickets?' 'I meant to, but he'd already left, so I gave them to his sister, who's going to pass them on.'
quests.ruleExplanation: Look closely: 'them' is what was handed over and will be passed on. The tickets are plural; Tariq and his sister are people.
quests.nativeTip: What was given to the sister?

quests.contextSentence: 'Have you spoken to Hana or Jun about the rota?' 'I spoke to Hana. She said Jun had swapped the shifts, but he says he never touched them.'
quests.ruleExplanation: The pronoun 'them' is plural and follows 'touched'. The shifts are what was allegedly swapped.
quests.nativeTip: What could Jun have touched, or swapped?

quests.contextSentence: 'Which of your neighbours complained?' 'The ones whose dog I walk. They said it barks when I leave it in the garden.'
quests.ruleExplanation: Note that 'it' is non-human and is the subject of 'barks'. The dog is the one that barks; the garden is where it is left.

quests.contextSentence: The two sisters, who had not spoken for years, met at their mother's funeral, where each blamed herself for the silence.
quests.ruleExplanation: Remember that 'herself' is singular, so it follows 'each', taking the sisters one at a time. It is not their mother.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'herself' points back to ➔ 'each of the sisters'

quests.contextSentence: After the surgeon had spoken to the family, she asked the nurse to give them a few minutes alone.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Them' is plural and is the object of 'give'. The people who were spoken to, the family, are those who need time.
quests.nativeTip: Who needs a few minutes alone?

quests.contextSentence: The judge reminded the jurors that the defendant, who had chosen to represent himself, was entitled to question the witnesses.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Himself' follows 'who had chosen to represent', and 'who' is the defendant. So the defendant is representing himself.

quests.contextSentence: The neighbours whose extension the council had approved told the builders they would pay for the scaffolding themselves.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Themselves' emphasises who will pay. The neighbours are the ones whose extension it is, so they pay, not the builders.

quests.contextSentence: The board asked the auditor to explain the discrepancy, which she attributed to a system change the finance team had failed to document, though it had been announced.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Though' contrasts 'failed to document' with 'announced'. The thing that was announced but not documented is the system change.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'it' points back to ➔ 'the system change'

quests.contextSentence: The ambassadors, who had been briefed by their aides, told reporters that neither of them would comment until each had spoken to his own government.
quests.ruleExplanation: Notice that 'his' is singular, so it goes with 'each'. It is one ambassador's own government, not that of the aides or reporters.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'his' points back to ➔ 'each of the ambassadors'
